bill.title: A bill to amend the Food Security Act of 1985 to add the emergency watershed program as a covered program for purposes of carrying out the regional conservation partnership program, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would amend the Food Security Act of 1985 to include the Emergency Watershed Program as an eligible program under the Regional Conservation Partnership Program. The change would allow watershed emergency projects to be coordinated with other conservation efforts through the partnership framework. The bill appears narrowly focused on this administrative adjustment to conservation program eligibility.

industries.rationale: The bill modifies conservation partnership programs that directly affect farming and ranching operations participating in watershed and land conservation efforts.
Emergency watershed programs typically involve infrastructure work such as erosion control, flood prevention structures, and land stabilization projects.
Watershed programs address water quality and management issues that overlap with water utility and watershed management operations.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
